name: NMDC Limited
reason: State-owned iron-ore miner whose earnings follow ore prices and government royalty policy: EBIT margin fell from 57.7% (2020) to 27.9%, EPS fell 36% in 2022, and FY2/FY3 consensus growth is only 6.3%/4.9%.

name: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd
reason: Cyclical automaker with losses in 2019-21 and 2025 (EPS -4.43 INR), a 10-yr average ROE of -0.5%, and JLR/EV execution risk; no durable economics.

name: Chambal Fertilisers & Chemicals Ltd.
reason: Urea earnings are set by the government subsidy and gas-pricing regime, and EPS of 48.6 INR is at its 10-yr high while consensus FY2 is -8.5%; it is cheap but not special.

name: Indian Bank
reason: PSU bank at peak EPS (90.1 INR, 1.0x 10-yr max) after recovering from bad loans; 10-yr average ROE of 10.1% and share count up 10.9%/yr from merger and recapitalisation dilution fail the US bank standard.

name: Life Insurance Corp. of India
reason: Government-controlled life insurer with a short listed record (IPO 2022); EPS of 45.4 INR depends on par-fund surplus transfers and state policy, 10-yr average ROE is 4.7%, and FY1 consensus is only +3.6%.

name: Gujarat Energy Ltd
reason: State-linked city-gas distributor whose margins follow LNG and APM gas prices: EPS was flat at about 14 INR in 2023-24 before jumping to 25.4, FY2 consensus is -0.2%, and LTG is 4%.

name: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Limited
reason: Holding company over Chola Investment & Finance and Chola MS General Insurance with a persistent holdco discount; consolidated EPS swings (5.0 to 130 INR) reflect subsidiary consolidation, and its value depends on a credit cycle it does not control.

name: Can Fin Homes Ltd.
reason: Plain-vanilla salaried home-loan lender with EPS up 8 of 10 years (11.8 to 81.5 INR, 21% 10-yr CAGR), a worst year of only -2.4% through IL&FS, COVID and rate cycles, about 20% average ROE, zero M&A and FY2/FY3 consensus of +13%; deep dive to check the Canara Bank (PSU) promoter stake and the 2023 branch fraud.

name: IIFL Finance Limited
reason: RBI imposed a gold-loan embargo in 2024 for compliance failures, cutting EPS 66% (47.5 to 15.9 INR); governance and regulatory risk fail the Buffett test.

name: Hindalco Industries Limited
reason: Aluminium and copper earnings follow LME prices: EPS fell 31% in 2019, margin is at the 82nd percentile, and the acquisition-to-FCF ratio is 1.07x (Novelis/Aleris), so it is a commodity, M&A-led grower.

name: JM Financial Limited
reason: Earnings come from investment banking, wholesale and distressed credit, so they are tied to capital-markets activity; 10-yr EPS CAGR is 9.5% with a -22.7% year, and average ROE is 10.7%.

name: Sammaan Capital Ltd
reason: Former Indiabulls Housing: EPS collapsed from 84.5 to 22.9 INR after the 2018 wholesale real-estate book unwound, and the record includes governance and related-party controversies and net debt/EBITDA of 37x.

name: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank Ltd.
reason: Microfinance-heavy SFB with a 2021 loss and EPS down 46% from its peak (6.54 to 3.51 INR) in the current MFI stress; credit-cycle earnings with about 10% average ROE.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Limited
reason: Strong affordable-housing record (EPS 2.3 to 18.8 INR since 2018, 8/9 growth years, about 16.5% ROE, about 19% consensus), but it has been listed only since 2021 and its self-employed low-income borrowers have not been tested in a soft market, the same treatment as the US short-record names.

name: Muthoot Finance Ltd
reason: Best-in-class gold lender (28.7% 10-yr EPS CAGR, 23.5% ROE), but FY25 EPS nearly doubled (129.5 to 252.4 INR) on a record gold price with margin at the 91st percentile, and RBI gold-loan rule changes are pending, so peak earnings cannot be normalised with confidence.

name: Bandhan Bank Ltd.
reason: Microfinance-concentrated bank whose EPS fell 94% in 2021 and 55% in 2025 (17.0 to 7.6 INR) on East-India MFI credit cycles; 5-yr EPS CAGR is -11%, and it is not forecastable.

name: NLC India Limited
reason: State-owned lignite and thermal generator with tariff-set returns, negative FCF from heavy capex (FCF conversion -0.81), net debt/EBITDA of 4.35x, and long-term coal transition risk.

name: State Bank of India
reason: State-controlled bank at peak EPS (87.6 INR, 1.0x max) with a 2017 loss and 10-yr average ROE of 9.5%; it fails the US bank standard (BAC/MTB precedent), and policy-directed lending adds risk.

name: E.I.D.-Parry (India) Limited
reason: Sugar and distillery earnings are set by cane pricing and the government ethanol policy, and consolidated profit mainly reflects its Coromandel stake; EPS is lumpy (2.2 to 49.6 to 32.2 INR) with a 43% adj-vs-GAAP gap.

name: CESC Ltd
reason: RP-Sanjiv Goenka regulated Kolkata utility: 5-yr EPS CAGR is 4.4% (9.46 to 11.76 INR), net debt/EBITDA is 4.5x and FCF conversion is 0.13; regulated returns fall below the 7% growth bar.
